newsitem.title: USA: Briefing on Korea talks proposal set for Jan. 29.
newsitem.headline: Briefing on Korea talks proposal set for Jan. 29.

text.p: U.S. and South Korean officials will brief North Korea on Jan. 29 on a proposal for four-party talks to consider the future of the Korean peninsula, the State Department said on Thursday.

Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said no venue had yet been agreed, but other officials said it was most likely to be New York, where Pyongyang has a U.N. mission and where U.S.-North Korean talks have taken place in the past.

"We are looking forward to these talks because we want to proceed with the peace treaty for the Korean peninsula," Burns told reporters. The 1950-53 Korean war ended only with an armistice, which is still in place.
The proposal for four-party talks, grouping the two Koreas, the United States and China, was launched last April by U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam.
Communist North Korea has not formally responded to the proposal. But it has agreed to the briefing as part of a string of agreements with the United States.
Late last month, North Korea issued a statement of regret over an incident in September in which a North Korean submarine beached on a southern shore, disgorging armed commandos.
That triggered U.S. approval of new food aid to flood-stricken North Korea and South Korean agreement to proceed with supply of new nuclear reactors to Pyongyang.
The briefing is seen as significant in that it will involve South Korean as well as U.S. officials. Past pledges by North Korea to improve relations with the South have so far led to little change.
